A fair trial is a NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:3513 5 CRR-5786-2025 part of the right guaranteed to an accused under Article 21 of the Constitution.
sentences._hearing_file: Rohit vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 February, 2026.json

sentences.text: The right to a fair trial of the accused includes the right to defend.
sentences._hearing_file: Rohit vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 February, 2026.json

Discretion to defer Cross-Examination (Section 231(2); The Judge has the power to:
*Defer the cross-examination of any witness until other witnesses are examined.

*
Recall any witness for further cross- examination.

opennyai_summary.21_July_2023__facts:
This is the first application filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No. 54/2023, registered at Police Station-Lanji, District Balaghat (MP) for the offence under Sections 21(1), 21(2), 21(3) of Banning of Unregulated Deposit Scheme Act and Section 420, 406 and 120-B of Indian Penal Code.
Complainant was lured to deposit an amount of Rs. 1 lac and promise was made that this amount will be doubled within short period of time.
It is submitted that there is two more criminal antecedents against applicant.
Applicant alongwith others used to lure innocent villagers to double the money and has received an amount of Rs. 1 lac and has given cheque of Rs. 2 lacs.
No investment was ever made by applicant and no chit and fund company was existing.
Offence under Sections 21(1), 21(2), 21(3) of Banning of Unregulated Deposit Scheme Act is also registered against him.

6. Considering aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting on the merits of the case, bail application filed by applicant is allowed on following conditions :
1. Applicant will deposit Rs. 1,00,000/- (Rs. One Lac Only) under protest before trial Court.
Amount deposited by applicant shall be kept in FDR and same will be subject to final judgment which will be passed by the trial Court.
2 . Applicant will mark his presence before local police station on 1st of every month till completion of trial.
3. If applicant is found involved in any other offence in future during bail, then Public Prosecutor/APP is at liberty to file an application for cancellation of bail and trial Court will consider the same and cancel the bail, if allegations are found to be true.
7. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on aforesaid conditions on furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only) with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his regular appearance before Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of trial on aforesaid conditions.
8. The applicant shall also abide by the following conditions of Section 437 (3) of Cr. P. C. as under:-
(a) that such person shall attend in accordance with the conditions of the bond executed under this Chapter;
(b) that such person shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected of the commission of which he is suspected and;
(c) that such person shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

The charges were framed on 12.02.2022 and at the stage of prosecution evidence, the revision petitioner and co-accused Neha Sharma filed two application on 26.09.2023, i.e. one application was under Section 91 of Cr.P.C., 1973 for the documents mentioned in para no.2 to 12 to be summoned submitting that they are in possession of complainant party.
4. The application under Section 91 of Cr.P.C., 1973 is rejected on the ground that the documents mentioned in the application under Section 91 of Cr.P.C., 1973 are not part of the final report/charge-sheet and at the stage of prosecution evidence, the application under Section 91 of Cr.P.C., 1973, is not tenable.
5. The application under Section 231(2) of Cr.P.C., 1973 is rejected on the ground that in the fact of this case, it is not required that the cross- examination be conduced after recording the examination in chief of the witnesses.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
An earlier case, namely Om Prakash Sharma v CBI, Delhi, (2000) 5 SCC 679 was also taken note of in Sarla Gupta (supra) as below:
'48.
As held by this Court, the object is to ensure that the accused has knowledge of the documents, objects, etc. in the custody of the investigating officer which are not relied upon so that at the appropriate stage, the accused can apply by invoking the provisions of Section 91CrPC (Section 94 BNSS)
for providing copies of the documents which are not relied upon by the prosecution.
At the stage of entering upon defence, an accused can apply for the issue of process for the production of any document or thing in accordance with Section 233(3)CrPC [Section 256(3)
BNSS].
A fair trial is a NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:3513 5 CRR-5786-2025 part of the right guaranteed to an accused under Article 21 of the Constitution.
The right to a fair trial of the accused includes the right to defend.
The right to defend consists of the right to lead the defence evidence by examining the witnesses and producing the documents.
Therefore, the accused is entitled to exercise his right at the stage of entering upon defence by compelling the prosecution or a third party to produce a document or a thing in their possession or custody.
The court can decline the request of the accused for issuing process for the production of documents only on the limited grounds set out in sub-section (3) of Section 233CrPC.
Accordingly, the learned trial Court has not committed any illegality in rejecting the application under section 91 of Cr.P.C., 1973, at the stage of prosecution evidence.
Since,
in this case, it is not stated that the referred documents are not in possession of Investigating Officer, accordingly, the revision petitioner has to clarified that the sought documents are in whose possession and thereafter, he may pray for calling the aforesaid documents by mentioning specifically the name of the person from whose possession, the revision petitioner want to summon/produce the documents.

11. Hence, the provision of Section 231(2) of Cr.P.C., 1973 is in the discretion of the trial judge to permit the cross-examination of the witnesses to be deferred until other witnesses are examined or recall any witness for further cross-examination.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
12. Accordingly, no illegality has committed by learned trial Court in exercising the discretion under Section 231(2) of Cr.P.C., 1973.
The criminal revision stands rejected.
